# W35: Tooling: F47 edits U16's paper/main.tex, and board_rows.py passes ruff UP017
**GitHub issue:** none; a file ticket, never published as an issue
**Status:** draft
Brief:
Make F47's ticket say it edits U16's `paper/main.tex` rather than creating it, so `paper/` has one owner (ledger R08-M3), and fix ruff UP017 in `.agents/skills/factory-watch/board_rows.py`.
Where: `docs/tickets/F47-paper-placeholders.md`, `.agents/skills/factory-watch/board_rows.py`, `tests/test_paper_owner.py` (new).
Done means: no clause of F47's Where or Except line that says (new) or creates names a tracked file, while its Where line still names `paper/main.tex`; `bin/check_tickets.py` passes; `ruff check --select UP017` on `board_rows.py` exits 0; the trace row W35 has a check; the gate stays green.
Out of scope: the F71 canary steps, F47's own work and done checks, any file under `paper/`.
Track: B    Risk: low    Mode: build    Open question: none
Work item: W35 of the implementation plan, section 6.2, batch 2 (U16 tooling); runs: the Loam factory from `~/distbench-isc`; Proven: D.
Base: `isc-build@a15f43056393c59836e0d54d7283a68ff5618776` (group 2 landed, U16 included; tip as last fetched on the Mac, 10 Nov); the run's real base is the round-0 sha in its `factory.log`, which must hold W07.
Size: 1-2 agent-hours (estimate: the plan's 2-3 h less the canary steps, which are the lead's and Samyak's; a text edit, a one-line fix and one test).
Blocked by: W07, J08

## Goal and why
The blind review of the build plan found `paper/` with two owners (R08-M3): U16 added `paper/main.tex` on `isc-build`, and F47 still says it creates that file, so a run of F47 would overwrite U16's paper.
UP017 is the one ruff finding U16 left in a file outside the gate's lint scope.
Ledger ids closed: R08-M3. Trace ids its checks prove: W35 (docs/tickets/trace.tsv).

## Do not touch
The standing list.
Also: `src/`, `tasks/`, `agent/`, `experiments/`, `paper/`, `pyproject.toml`.
Except: `docs/tickets/F47-paper-placeholders.md` and `.agents/skills/factory-watch/board_rows.py` (this ticket edits them), and `tests/test_paper_owner.py` (this ticket creates it).

## Out of scope
The F71 canary steps 2-5 (Decisions): they are the lead's and Samyak's.
F47's own work, its done-checks block and its status line.
`bin/check_tickets.py`, `bin/done-checks` and the README rows, which the plan gives this item's owner but which need no change here.

## Approach
In F47, put the files it edits and the files it creates in separate clauses joined by `; `: on the Where line, `paper/main.tex` as U16's file that F47 edits, then F47's new files with (new); on the Except line, the same split, with "this ticket creates them" only after the new files.
Make F47's Brief line and its Approach sentence on `paper/main.tex` (today "`paper/main.tex` is an `article` skeleton ...") say F47 adds the `db.tex` and `values.tex` inputs and the `\db{...}` uses to U16's `paper/main.tex`, keeping U16's content: both name it in those words, "U16's `paper/main.tex`", and neither calls it a skeleton or an `article` (U16's paper is IEEEtran); change nothing else in F47.
In `board_rows.py`, apply ruff's UP017 fix: `from datetime import UTC, datetime` and `datetime.now(UTC)` (the module imports the `datetime` class, so `datetime.UTC` would raise).
Add `tests/test_paper_owner.py` (new): one test, marked `pytest.mark.proves("W35", fails_on="a15f4305", symptom="F47 says it creates paper/main.tex, which U16 already added")`, that reads F47 at `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "docs/tickets/F47-paper-placeholders.md"` and fails when a clause of F47's Where or Except line that says (new) or creates names `paper/main.tex`, the one file U16 owns; run it once on F47 as it stood at `a15f4305` (`git show a15f4305:docs/tickets/F47-paper-placeholders.md` in a scratch tree) and keep its failing output in decisions.md; it must not test F47's other files, which F47's own branch adds and tracks.

**Working rules when the work gets hard** (TOOLKIT section 5).
- Fail first: before the first edit, run every done check or Acceptance command on the base commit or planted edit this ticket names, and keep the output.
  Each non-guard check must fail with the symptom the ticket predicts, and each regression guard must give the base result the ticket records; any other result is a ticket defect: stop and report it, and never edit the check.
- Diagnose: for a failure whose cause you do not know, read `principle-fix-root-causes` and build the smallest command that fails on it, off the pair and the GPU when it reproduces there.
  Write that command and its output down before any fix, and fix the first place the state goes wrong, not the symptom.
- Stuck: when two fixes resting on one premise fail the same check, read `principle-attack-the-premise` and test the premise itself before a third attempt.
  In a factory run, consult the advisor tool before the third attempt; if the check cannot be met, write `ABANDON NAME reason` in decisions.md and stop.
  Attended, after a third failure on one item, stop and give the lead the evidence; the lead may rerun at xhigh or brief `escalate`.
- Second opinion (attended): before a choice that is costly to undo (a contract shape, a public interface, a frozen-check edit, one of several designs), ask the lead for a blind read by Codex read-only or `escalate`, given the artifact and its constraints, never your reasoning.
  When the same infrastructure failure returns after one fix, or the approach costs more than the goal is worth, ask the lead for a surprise-me pass aimed at this ticket's goal.
- Prove: prove a runner, agent command, package, oracle, orchestrator or grader change with `.agents/skills/verify-distbench/SKILL.md`, driving the real command line beside a control that fails.
  A change to a function `.agents/skills/formal-orchestrator/SKILL.md` maps runs its `tlc-check` and follows its DRIFT steps.
  Read `principle-prove-it-works` before you say done, `blast-radius` on a runner, grader or orchestrator change, and `benchmark-checklist` before you report any time.
  In a factory run these proofs live in the done checks, because your own shell is sandboxed.
  A step run on a stand-in (the local executor, a fake backend, the Mac) stays UNVERIFIED until it runs on its real target.
- Evidence: keep each command with its exit code and output in this ticket's evidence folder; in a factory run the supervisor's check output and decisions.md are the evidence, so mark anything they do not show as unverified.
  Long or live work keeps a `show-me-your-work` decision log; report under the seven headings of `docs/WORKERS.md`, ending with a READY line (host, exit code, log path).
- Never: edit, weaken or route around a done check or anything under `docs/tickets/checks/`; push or merge `main`; rent or make a paid call; launch a factory run (the lead does); kill a process by name or pattern; run a GPU, Docker or MPI job on jhaveris without its `flock` lock; open a FREEZE file.
- pstack: the router (`sam-cc-setup:pstack`) picks the method; a factory ticket's `skills:` line names only a skill that overrides its pick.

For this ticket: the F71 canary steps under Decisions are not this run's work; they publish an issue at `ready-for-agent` and run `next` on the main clone `~/distbench`, which only Samyak and the lead do, only after his one merge to `main` (rulings-log 76, c2), and never in `~/distbench-isc`.

## Done checks

predict trace-rows python3 bin/check_trace.py --batch 2 2>&1 | grep -qE '^rule [^ ]+ has no check \(batch [0-9]+, closer ([^)]*, )?W35(,|\))'
out=$(python3 -c 'import re, subprocess; t = open("docs/tickets/F47-paper-placeholders.md").read().splitlines(); tracked = set(subprocess.run(["git", "ls-files"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split()); bad = sorted({p for l in t if l.startswith(("Where:", "Except:")) for c in l.split(";") if re.search(r"\(new\)|creates", c) for p in re.findall(r"`([^`]+)`", c) if p in tracked}); where = next((l for l in t if l.startswith("Where:")), ""); brief = t[t.index("Brief:") + 1] if "Brief:" in t else ""; print("claims-new", bad, "main-in-where", "`paper/main.tex`" in where, "skeleton", any("paper/main.tex" in l and ("skeleton" in l or "`article`" in l) for l in t), "u16-brief", "U16'"'"'s `paper/main.tex`" in brief, "u16-lines", sum("U16'"'"'s `paper/main.tex`" in l for l in t) >= 2)' 2>&1); chk=$(python3 bin/check_tickets.py 2>&1); crc=$?; [ "$out" = "claims-new [] main-in-where True skeleton False u16-brief True u16-lines True" ] && [ "$crc" = 0 ] && pass f47-paths || fail f47-paths "in docs/tickets/F47-paper-placeholders.md no clause of the Where or Except line that says (new) or creates may name a tracked file, while Where still names paper/main.tex, which F47 edits; no line may still call paper/main.tex a skeleton or an article to write; the Brief line and one more line (the Approach sentence) must name U16's \`paper/main.tex\`; and bin/check_tickets.py must pass: $(tail -c 300 <<<"$out" | tr "\n" " "); check_tickets rc $crc $(tail -c 300 <<<"$chk" | tr "\n" " ")"
b=.agents/skills/factory-watch/board_rows.py; d=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/w35.XXXXXX") || d=/nonexistent; out=$(ruff check --select UP017 "$b" 2>&1); rc=$?; run=$(python3 "$b" . /dev/null "$d" 2>&1); rrc=$?; [ "$rc" = 0 ] && [ "$rrc" = 0 ] && grep -qE '^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z rows=' <<<"$run" && pass up017 || fail up017 "ruff check --select UP017 on $b must exit 0, and the script must still run (python3 $b . /dev/null <dir> prints its time-stamped summary line): ruff rc $rc $(tail -c 300 <<<"$out" | tr "\n" " "); run rc $rrc $(grep -v " rows=" <<<"$run" | tail -c 200 | tr "\n" " ")"
out=$(python3 bin/check_trace.py --batch 2 2>&1); rc=$?; miss=$(grep -E '^rule [^ ]+ has no check \(batch [0-9]+, closer ([^)]*, )?W35(,|\))|^check tests/test_paper_owner\.py' <<<"$out"); { [ "$rc" = 0 ] || [ "$rc" = 1 ]; } && ! grep -q "^Traceback" <<<"$out" && [ -z "$miss" ] && pass trace-rows || fail trace-rows "the docs/tickets/trace.tsv row W35 needs a check that proves it (pytest.mark.proves with fails_on and symptom), and this ticket's test must raise no check problem: rc $rc; $(tr '\n' ' ' <<<"${miss:-$out}" | cut -c1-500)"
out=$(guard bin/check 2>&1); rc=$?; last=$(tail -n 1 <<<"$out"); { [ -n "${LOAM_HOOK:-}" ] || { [ "$rc" = 0 ] && [ "$last" = "check: PASSED" ]; }; } && pass check-green || fail check-green "bin/check must exit 0 and end 'check: PASSED' (a sandbox run is not the gate): rc $rc, last line: $last"

### How we build
> **How we build (DistBench ISC build, rulings of 10 Nov 2026, items 27-58).**
> - Iterate to a correct version; there are no internal gates, and the one internal date is the last core grade by Mon 7 Dec (item 63).
>   The one registration is the protocol entries, made the moment the rehearsal checks pass.
> - An attended ticket starts from the `isc-build` commit it names; a factory run's base is the round-0 commit in its `factory.log`.
>   Cite functions by name, never by line number.
> - Integration is by script: the integration lane lands a pushed branch on `isc-build` only when the contract tests and the gate pass on the merged tree; a gate is green only with exit 0 and the last line `check: PASSED`.
>   Nobody merges by hand.
>   The plan's section 7 sets the landing order and the edit order of `orchestrator.py`, `runner.py` and `grader.py`.
> - A contract changes only through its owner (plan section 3).
>   Contract tests are frozen checks in docs/tickets/checks/contracts/; only the lead edits their open.txt, at landing.
> - Start no new item while landings wait longer than two gate runs.
> - The factory runs file tickets only, from the second clone `~/distbench-isc` on jhaveris.
>   Never use issue mode, never label an issue `ready-for-agent`, never run `next` there.
>   Run `bin/factory -C ~/distbench-isc lint <ticket>` (exit code) before release; the lead launches each run.
>   The launcher pushes each finished run as `build/f-<id>` and adds its row to the integration list.
>   A factory worker's own shell is always sandboxed; its done checks, which the supervisor runs, reach Docker and the full gate.
> - The build runs in a Claude Code session on jhaveris (item 50).
>   The lead's rule, Samyak's to overrule: a ticket written there takes an id J01 onward, uses this form and these blocks, gets a ledger row, and is committed on the build branch; a change to a ruling, a registered rule, a frozen check, money or a rental goes to Samyak first.
> - jhaveris: build sessions run with the sandbox off (item 31) and reach the gate by ssh.
>   Heavy work runs inside the build memory slice W04 sets up; until W04 lands, at most 2 factory runs and one MPI test at a time.
>   While calibration or confirmatory sessions run, the build slice is shrunk so the sessions' `memory` fits beside it; the orchestrator refuses a launch that does not fit (W13 part (i)).
>   Take locks with `flock` only, in the order gate, gpu, mpi (`gate-0.lock`, `gate-1.lock`, `gpu.lock`, `mpi-0.lock`, `mpi-1.lock` in `~/.local/state/distbench/`); never pkill by pattern.
